newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED LARGELY STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED LARGELY STABLE.

text.p: HARARE, June 19 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mainly stable on Thursday, dealers said.

The market opened with a Z$198.9 million surplus from Wednesday and the central Reserve Bank, forecasting another surplus for Thursday, sold Z$600 million worth of 91-day treasury bills at a discount of 25 percent compared to 24.99 percent the previous day.
The central bank bills were changing hands on the secondary market at a steady 24.5 percent.
Call money was also quoted stable at 22 percent, as were bankers acceptance bills at 25.5 percent (buying) and 24.5 percent (selling).
The buying rate for 30-, 60- and 90-day NCD bills edged up to 26.5 from 26 percent, but they were being sold unchanged from Wednesday's 25 percent.
